articles.title: Actor Rob Schneider claims Texas is under a 'Marxist and Islamic threat'
articles.description: MAGA-aligned American actor Rob Schneider publicly attacked Texas Republican leadership Monday, claiming the state has been seized by Islamic law. In a social media pos t, Schneider alleged that organizations with "terror ties" receive nonprofit status while Texas remains complicit through taxpayer funding of "madrasas." He accused the state of harboring "Sharia courts, Sharia judges, and Sharia patrols" that remain unopened. Schneider, known for promoting medical misinformation and bogus health cures, specifically targeted Gov. Greg Abbott, Attorney General Ken Paxton, and other GOP leaders. "I never thought I would watch the Islamic and Marxist threat seize large parts of our great nation," Schneider wrote . He claimed the damage mirrors Europe's experience and is now "unfolding" across America. Schneider's allegations reflect long-propagated conspiracy theories about Islamic takeovers targeting immigrant communities in Texas, including recent moral panic over an Islamic water park event in North Texas. articles.title: 'They're in danger': Insiders reveal which Trump agency has Iranians feeling 'scared'
articles.description: President Donald Trump doesn't seem to have much sway in the negotiations to end the war against Iran, but there is someone else who may hold the key, insiders revealed on Monday. Axios reported , citing multiple anonymous White House officials, that Iranian officials seem more afraid of the U.S. Treasury than of the Department of Defense. The insiders argued that Iranians are more afraid of sanctions now because of the country's economic conditions. "The Iranians want to stop being bombed, and they want money," a senior administration official told the outlet. "But that's almost in reverse order. They really want the money first." That seems to give Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent significant leverage over how the war negotiations proceed, according to the officials. "They're in danger of runs on banks. There are gasoline shortages in this giant oil-rich country," one official told Axios. "They're more scared of Treasury than the War Department." "The president has a win-win optionality. The U.S. is capable of prosecuting this militarily to the fullest extent. And the U.S. is capable of exerting economic sanctions that cripple Iran," another official said.

articles.title: Kash Patel personally put The Atlantic 'on notice' over drinking claims: court docs
articles.description: FBI Director Kash Patel was behind threats made to stop claims about his drinking habits from becoming public, newly released documents reveal. Attorney Jesse Binnall sent a letter to The Atlantic hours before it published the story on April 17, 2026, demanding the outlet not publish. The Atlantic published anyway. Three days later, Patel filed suit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia seeking $250 million. The threats emerged in court documents filed July 27. Among the demands in the letter was an ultimatum. "Accordingly, should The Atlantic choose to publish this demonstrably false and defamatory article, Director Patel will have no choice but to take swift legal action to uphold his reputation," Binnall wrote . "With this letter, you are also on notice of your ongoing obligations to preserve documents related to Director Patel," the letter said, also accusing The Atlantic of running "an ongoing campaign to damage his reputation." The story Patel wanted to kill reported that he was known to " drink to the point of obvious intoxication " at private clubs in Washington, D.C., and Las Vegas. The Atlantic reported that sources said his drinking had "negatively impacted various law-enforcement investigations" — including the murder of Charlie Kirk — and that his "drinking has been a recurring source of concern across the government." The documents show that behind the scenes, the Trump administration was scrambling to contain the damage. Sarah Fitzpatrick, who reported the story, had already heard from FBI assistant director Ben Williamson on publication day that the story was "...one of the most absurd things I've ever read." "He has accomplished more in 14 months than the previous administration did in four years," acting Attorney General Todd Blanche wrote in a statement to The Atlantic. "Anonymously sourced hit pieces do not constitute journalism." White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Patel "remains a critical player on the Administration's law and order team" — also without refuting a single claim. In court documents filed July 27, The Atlantic argued the complaint "does not allege a single fact showing that any statement in the Article is false" and called several claims "substantially true" — backed by congressional testimony, public lawsuits by fired FBI agents, and oversight letters from Democratic lawmakers. The Atlantic's attorneys noted the suit is Patel's fifth defamation action against media outlets, all of which have been dismissed or dropped. His previous suit — against an MS NOW contributor who said Patel spent more time at nightclubs than at FBI headquarters — was dismissed the day after Patel filed this one.

articles.title: James Carville calls on Dem activist to 'take over' DNC
articles.description: Democratic strategist James Carville recommended gun control activist David Hogg as a replacement for Democratic National Committee, or DNC, chair Ken Martin, citing organizational dysfunction and financial turmoil. Speaking from his recovery bed on his podcast , Politicon, Carville said, "If David Hogg wants to take it over, then, I ain't stopping you, go ahead, man," according to The Daily Beast . Carville acknowledged the DNC's well-documented problems, explaining, "It's dysfunctional. It's just difficult to do anything with it. And it's all true." The New York Times reported Sunday, Martin has become increasingly isolated. Its report described a phone-throwing incident with a junior aide that triggered an HR complaint. The DNC also faces $2 million in debt while vendors have been asked to delay billing until after midterms. Despite favorable political conditions, internal distrust, a failed 2024 election autopsy, and widening cash gaps with Republicans have raised concerns about Martin's leadership effectiveness and the party's organizational viability. Hogg, 26, became known for surviving the 2018 Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting in Parkland, Florida. Since then, he served as DNC vice chair between February and June 2025, before his election was discarded after a clash over his push to primary incumbent Democrats. Watch the video below. articles.title: John Cornyn teases revolt against Trump after primary betrayal
articles.description: Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX), defeated in May's GOP primary by a Trump-endorsed opponent, is leveraging his "newfound political freedom." Punchbowl News reported Monday that Cornyn aims to extract concessions from the White House or obstruct its agenda. Cornyn's primary target is shuttering the Trump administration's $1.7 billion anti-weaponization fund , which provides payouts to those claiming unfair targeting by former President Joe Biden's Justice Department. Cornyn suggested Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's confirmation could be jeopardized unless the White House capitulates on the fund. "If they want to get [Blanche] out of the committee, I think they realize they need to talk to us," Cornyn said. Already freed from primary threats, Cornyn previously leveraged ambassador nominees to secure international AIDS relief funding commitments. He promised, "You ain't seen nothing yet," according to Punchbowl News. Cornyn joins growing GOP "apostates," or ousted lawmakers with nothing to lose by opposing Trump, according to The Washington Post's Karen Tumulty. Watch the video below. articles.title: Trump Poll Collapse Hits New Milestone as Leaks Reveal Fresh GOP Panic
articles.description: Donald Trump has hit a trifecta, throwing away the traditional GOP edge on the economy, immigration, and national security. The latest polls show Democrats are leading Republicans on the economy by a comfortable nine points, have hit near-parity with the GOP on immigration , and lead on foreign policy , even as Trump has sunk into the 20s on the Iran war, all shockers. T hese polls show it’s all driven by Trump’s collapsing approval on all three. Yet Trump just unleashed a huge new wave of tariffs. His GOP allies are leaking their deep dismay to Politico : One suggests this worsens the affordability problem and cannot be spun favorably by GOP candidates. Another says this is a “bad conversation for Republicans.” We talked to Democratic strategist Andrew Bates. He explains what all this looks like on the ground in difficult House races, what obstacles still remain, and why it remains hard for Democrats to win rural voters who are unhappy with Trump. Listen to this episode here .
